claims.value: other: flattened and branched squamous cell
claims.quote: A squamous pulmonary alveolar epithelial cell that is flattened and branched.
This large cell has thin (50-100 nm) cytoplasmic extensions to form the air-blood barrier essential for normal gas exchange.

claims.value: thin, elastic basement membrane that the epithelium is attached to
claims.quote: The simple squamous epithelium formed by type I alveolar cells is attached to a thin, elastic basement membrane.

claims.value: This large cell covers more than 98% of the alveolar surface, and its thin (50–100 nm) cytoplasmic extensions form the air-blood barrier that normal gas exchange depends on.
claims.quote: A pulmonary alveolar type 1 cell covers more than 98% of the alveolar surface. This large cell has thin (50-100 nm) cytoplasmic extensions to form the air-blood barrier essential for normal gas exchange.

claims.value: These squamous cells cover up to 97 percent of the alveolar surface yet are only about 25 nm thick, making a broad, very thin lining that is highly permeable to gases.
claims.quote: A type I alveolar cell is a squamous epithelial cell of the alveoli, which constitute up to 97 percent of the alveolar surface area. These cells are about 25 nm thick and are highly permeable to gases.

source.section: 22.1 Organs and Structures of the Respiratory System

claims.value: The extremely thin epithelium these cells form borders the capillary endothelium, and together they make a respiratory membrane about 0.5 μm thick that gases cross by simple diffusion.
claims.quote: This epithelium is extremely thin and borders the endothelial membrane of capillaries. Taken together, the alveoli and capillary membranes form a respiratory membrane that is approximately 0.5 μm (micrometers) thick. The respiratory membrane allows gases to cross by simple diffusion
